name: Repco Home Finance Limited
rating_outcome: [ICRA]AA- (Stable) / [ICRA]A1+; reaffirmed. Rated amounts marked 'to be confirmed by issuer' throughout - no sanction letters/term sheets supplied and no ICRA CORPORATE rationale for this issuer exists in the reference library (the only ICRA file found is a SECURITISATION rationale on the Pratham 12 2025 trust, on which RHFL is Originator only, not the rated obligor). Matches the company's own FY2025 AR disclosure (Note 32.17) and CareEdge's independently published AA-; Stable / A1+ (30-Sep-2025). Step 12b scorecard's own native formula chain independently reproduces AA- with ZERO divergence from the Step 13 judgment view.
delivery_scope: Rationale + ratio engine (28/28 tie-outs reconcile) + ratio Excel (Financial_Spreads, 4 tabs) + Step 12 LENDING model (Lending_Model.xlsx: Book_Build -> P_and_L -> Balance_Sheet -> Credit_Ratios -> Debt_Breakup -> Stress_Case, zero unresolved formula cells after fixing a genuine circular reference by pricing interest on opening rather than average debt) + Step 12b scorecard (native Inputs->Scorecard->Rating template, sector=HFC). check_sections.py PASS, all quality probes clean after two fixes (absence-claim evidence text added near the rated-amount and rating-history gaps; net-worth basis for gearing stated explicitly, tangible vs total net worth shown to differ by only 0.57%). STANDALONE basis (RHFL's only related entity, Repco Micro Finance Limited, is an equity-accounted ASSOCIATE at 0.85% of total assets, not a subsidiary). Key figures: AUM Rs 14,492 cr (FY2025, +7.2%), PAT Rs 439.44 cr (+11.4%), CRAR 37.09% vs 15% NHB minimum, gearing declining 3.94x(FY23)->3.36x(FY25)->3.01x(30-Jun-26), GNPA improving every year 7.0%(FY22)->2.67%(30-Jun-26 excl. int. accrued), PCR thin at 43.48%. Stress case (100bps credit cost, 75bps spread compression, zero growth, 5 years): gearing holds at 2.4-2.9x but return on average assets falls to 1.66-1.72%, BELOW CareEdge's own published 2.00% downgrade trigger - a genuine finding surfaced by the model, stated in the rationale's 'what could go wrong' paragraph.
method_notes: Securitisation-vs-corporate-rating trap (new failure pattern, related to FM10/FM29): the only ICRA reference-library file for this issuer name is 'Repco Home Finance Limited_25 Feb 2026_141196.md', which reads as a same-issuer corporate rationale by filename alone but is actually a securitisation rationale on the PRATHAM 12 2025 trust (RHFL as Originator/Servicer, [ICRA]AAA(SO)/[ICRA]AA-(SO) on the TRUST's notes, not RHFL's own facilities). Caught before drafting by reading the file's title and Summary-of-rating-action table, not assumed from the filename. FM31 applied: Q1FY2027 filing showed all drawn debt current/short-tenor at the FILING date but this was correctly NOT read as evidence of an absent long-term rating - the AR's own Note 32.17 confirms live long-term AA-(Stable) facilities. Routing confirmed via the NBFC methodology's own scope footnote ('...housing finance companies (HFCs)...unless stated otherwise'), since ICRA's dedicated HFC methodology (Sep 2019) is archived. FY2026 balance-sheet gap: no 31-Mar-2026 balance sheet exists in any of the 4 quarterly filings supplied (searched: 'Balance Sheet', 'Total Assets', 'Net Worth', 'Debt Equity' across all four) - only 30-Sep-2025 and 30-Jun-2026 balance sheets exist; FY2026 ratios needing a balance sheet are marked NA rather than interpolated, and the Step 12 model's FY2027E opens on the 30-Jun-2026 actuals with the resulting ~1.6%-of-book base-period overlap disclosed in the model's own header note.
